inputs.share_count_basis: 189.05m: shares on issue at 1 April 2025 was 187,410,632 (FY26 annual report equity note); FY26 year-end count per CSV is 187.97m; total shares increased to ~189.05m per an LTIP issuance disclosed 2026-07 (Analysis JSON recent_developments) -- using the most current actual count as fully diluted and held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count)
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T05:00:31Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API); 52-week range 0.81-2.89 NZD
inputs.wacc_rationale: 9.5% built on NZD risk-free ~4.5% (NZGB 10yr) + ERP ~5.0% adjusted for small-cap illiquidity and thin balance-sheet headroom; sits above the ~8-9% used for large-cap NZX names given the FY26 working-capital deficit, narrow covenant headroom (net leverage <=1.00x by Jun-26, interest cover >=4.00x) and activist/leadership disruption -- risk also carried in the wide bear/bull driver spread and 25% bear weight, not double-charged via a further WACC premium
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment A (leases as debt): lease principal ($2.0m FY26) and lease interest ($0.4m FY26) are NOT deducted from the flows (OCF/capex as reported already exclude them from the FCF walk since IFRS-16 principal sits in financing); lease liabilities (~$6.3m FY25, similar FY26) are added to net debt via the equity bridge rather than left in flows -- immaterial at ~3% of net debt so the choice barely moves the valuation, but stated for consistency
inputs.nci_treatment: None -- EROAD has no minority interests; Coretex NZ/USA and Imarda are 100%-owned subsidiaries
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing table: operating SaaS/hardware-subscription company). This is a first build (no prior memory entry, no prior DCF). FY26 NZ$134.7m goodwill/intangible impairment (North American CGU, Coretex acquisition) is entirely non-cash and sits in EBIT/NI only -- it does NOT touch OCF or capex, so reported_fcf (-2.2m) already excludes it; no further adjustment needed for the impairment itself. What DOES need adjusting: FY26 EBITDA (39.0m, 20.0% margin) is depressed ~$20.6m by one-off items (patent litigation $1.7m, net transformation costs $1.3m, $18.2m of non-cash accounting-estimate changes, $4.0m one-off 4G-related opex per Note 5) relative to FY25's 59.6m/30.7% -- base-case margin path starts near a partially-normalised ~24% (splitting the difference: crediting some but not all of the one-off relief, since NA cost pressure and lower operating leverage from the ARR decline are real, not one-off) and ramps to 29% by maturity as ANZ mix improves. FY26 capex (32.5m, 16.6% of revenue) is elevated by the now-88%-complete 4G hardware upgrade program (4G-related capex $14.3m FY26, $7.6m FY25 per management's own normalised-FCF reconciliation) -- capex_pct glides from 16.6% down to ~9% within 2 years as the program finishes, consistent with management's guided 'reported FCF should improve from FY27'. Net debt uses bank borrowings only ($26.1m: $5.0m current + $21.1m non-current term loans/RCF, Note 13) less cash ($10.1m) = $16.0m, matching the bear-case risk note in Analysis JSON and excluding ~$6m of lease liabilities (Treatment A, added via equity bridge instead). $108.5m of accumulated NZ tax losses (Note re tax losses, FY26 annual report) support a near-zero cash tax rate for several years -- cash_tax_rate_path held at 0% through the explicit years before stepping toward the 28% NZ statutory rate late in the horizon as losses are used up. Working capital: subscription/prepaid model with growing deferred revenue (33.3m FY26 vs 23.6m FY24) supports a modest positive wc_capture on revenue growth, but kept small (10%) given North America's revenue decline works against the group figure and management flagged FY26 OCF weakness from one-off costs. Horizon: 10 years, because FY26's owner-FCF margin is deeply depressed by one-off items and the 4G capex bulge -- a 5-year window would still be capitalising an unrepresentative, still-recovering margin. SBC is small (1.3% of revenue) -- included at 2.6/195.2=1.33% and held roughly flat as a % of revenue (LTI grants continue under the new CEO's incentive structure); house and street bases will sit close together given the small SBC base, unlike a US SaaS name. Base-case Y1 margin/capex path deliberately softened versus a mechanical snap-back: EBITDA margin starts FY27 near FY26's disrupted 20-21% level (new CEO does not start until Oct-26, so a full year of 'reset to execution' cost discipline should not be assumed from day one) and recovers over 2-3 years rather than immediately; capex normalises over 2 years (16.6% -> 13.0% -> 9.5%) rather than snapping to steady-state in year 1, since the 4G program still has ~12% of units outstanding at FY26 year-end.

equity_bridge.item: Lease liabilities (Treatment A, excluded from bank-debt net_debt figure)
equity_bridge.note: FY25 balance per Note 12 disclosure (5.6-6.3 range across FY25 filings); FY26 broadly similar magnitude, immaterial to per-share value

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (3yr -11.5%) is dominated by the FY26 non-cash impairment and is not a usable growth proxy for a capital-light SaaS business; EPS/FCF CAGRs are not meaningful given consecutive years of accounting losses (impairment, tax-benefit swings) and a reported-FCF series that swings on the 4G capex bulge rather than the underlying business. Revenue 3yr CAGR (3.7%, decelerating hard from the 16.3% 5yr figure as ARR turned slightly negative in FY26) is used as the growth anchor instead, consistent with management's own declined-to-guide stance for FY27.

base.narrative: ANZ (NZ + Australia, 62% of FY26 revenue) is the anchor: NZ delivers management's guided low-single-digit stable growth on its ~85-86% eRUC incumbency, Australia continues double-digit growth as the Cleanaway rollout completes (Nov-26) and the 'AU playbook' extends to other enterprise fleets. North America (38% of revenue) is managed to cash-flow neutrality rather than growth -- unit/ARR decline moderates but does not reverse within the explicit horizon. New CEO David Leach (starts Oct-26) executes the announced strategic reset broadly as described without a further governance or customer shock. EBITDA margin recovers from FY26's one-off-depressed 20.0% toward a mid-to-high-20s% mature level as patent-litigation and transformation costs (a one-off ~$3.0m combined) do not repeat, accounting-estimate volatility settles, and NA cost discipline bites, but does NOT return to FY25's 30.7% because North America's smaller, lower-margin revenue base persists. Capex normalises sharply once the 4G hardware upgrade (88% complete) finishes in FY27, per management's own guidance that reported FCF should improve from FY27. NZ universal eRUC legislation progresses through 2026 as flagged but its revenue impact is NOT explicitly modelled in the base case since the provider/collection model remains undecided -- it is optionality, not a base-case driver.

bull.narrative: NZ universal electronic RUC legislation passes in 2026 as targeted and EROAD retains a meaningful share of the expanded addressable market given its incumbency, providing an additional NZ growth leg not in the base case. Australia's Cleanaway win proves replicable and the 'AU playbook' lands several more enterprise logos, sustaining 30%+ ARR growth for several years. New CEO Leach repeats his Cin7 ARR-scaling playbook, and North America stabilises faster than guided (genuine modest growth returns by year 3 rather than mere neutrality) as the smaller, right-sized cost base proves competitive on price against Samsara/Geotab/Motive in specific verticals. The activist overhang (Ampfield) resolves constructively rather than as an ongoing distraction. Margin recovers past the FY25 pre-disruption level as AI-native operating leverage and the completed capitalisation-policy reset (R&D opex discipline) show through.

bear.narrative: North America's customer attrition continues beyond Old Dominion (asset retention already the weakest of the three regions at 80.1%) and 'cash-flow neutral' proves unachievable without further revenue base erosion, keeping group revenue flat-to-declining for several years. The four-month CEO vacancy and history of two departures in twelve months costs further execution momentum even after Leach starts, and the narrow June-2026 AGM margins (~67.5% turnout, resolutions passing with as little as ~70.6% support) presage renewed activist pressure or boardroom instability if early results disappoint, consuming management attention. NZ universal eRUC's collection/provider model is decided in a way that bypasses or dilutes EROAD's current incumbency (the company has itself publicly opposed an NZTA-as-retail-provider model, signalling this is a live risk, not a formality). Thin liquidity ($49.0m total, against a FY26 net working-capital deficit and covenants stepping down through the October 2027 facility maturity) forces a dilutive capital raise or asset sale within the horizon. Margin stays near FY26's disrupted level as North America's smaller revenue base and continued cost-to-serve pressure offset ANZ's better economics.

scenario_narratives.base: ANZ-led stabilisation: NZ steady, Australia scaling on Cleanaway, North America managed to cash-flow neutrality (not growth) under a new externally-hired CEO; margin partially recovers from FY26's one-off-depressed level; NZ universal eRUC treated as optionality, not baked into the numbers.
scenario_narratives.bull: Universal eRUC legislation passes and EROAD keeps its incumbency share; the Australia enterprise playbook repeats beyond Cleanaway; North America stabilises faster than guided; the new CEO repeats his Cin7 ARR-scaling record; margin recovers past pre-disruption FY25 levels.
scenario_narratives.bear: North America attrition continues past Old Dominion and cash-flow neutrality is missed; the CEO vacancy and narrow AGM result presage renewed activist/governance disruption; eRUC's provider model bypasses EROAD's incumbency; thin liquidity forces a dilutive raise.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight raised from the 15% house default to 25% given a genuine cluster of concurrent risks: withdrawn top-line guidance (a real visibility cut, not conservatism), a four-month CEO vacancy bridging into an unproven external hire, a contested board election that narrowly held (some resolutions ~70.6% support), a FY26 net working-capital deficit against covenants stepping down to October 2027, and North America's weakest-in-group 80.1% asset retention with no proof yet that 'cash-flow neutral' is achievable rather than aspirational. Bull weight trimmed to 25% (from 35%) because the bull case requires several largely independent things to go right simultaneously -- eRUC legislation AND a favourable collection-model outcome, Australia repeating Cleanaway-scale wins, AND North America outperforming its own modest neutrality target, AND a new CEO with no EROAD-specific track record delivering immediately.

valuation_philosophy.summary: EROAD is a turnaround-stage NZ SaaS/hardware-subscription telematics company entering FY27 with withdrawn top-line guidance, a completed but unproven leadership and governance reset, and a North American segment being deliberately shrunk to cash-flow neutrality after a large customer loss triggered a NZ$134.7m non-cash impairment. The valuation rests on ANZ's demonstrated free-cash-flow generation (NZ$19.5m normalised FCF from New Zealand + Australia combined in FY26) funding a North American business that no longer needs to grow, plus unquantified optionality from NZ's prospective universal electronic road-user-charging expansion. Reported FY26 owner FCF is negative, depressed by a near-complete 4G hardware upgrade program and a cluster of one-off costs (patent litigation, transformation, accounting-estimate changes) that together explain the gap to management's own NZ$14.4m normalised FCF figure -- the component build normalises both the margin and the capex path rather than extrapolating either the disrupted FY26 print or the flattering normalised figure uncritically.
key_risks_to_valuation: Withdrawn FY27 revenue/ARR guidance materially lowers forecast visibility versus the historical basis for this model
North America customer concentration: a single further large non-renewal could repeat the Old Dominion shock
New CEO (starts 12-Oct-2026) has no EROAD-specific track record; four-month leadership vacuum preceded his start
Activist shareholder (Ampfield, ~17%) narrowly failed to remove directors at the Jun-2026 AGM; renewed pressure is plausible if turnaround progress disappoints
FY26 net working-capital deficit and covenants (net leverage, interest cover) stepping down through October 2027 facility maturity leave thin headroom for further setbacks

NZ universal eRUC's eventual provider/collection model is undecided; EROAD's own public opposition to an NZTA-as-retail-provider model signals real uncertainty about whether incumbency converts into captured upside
